android.desc:
ReciPath is your kitchen companion. Plan meals from your own recipes, shop exactly what's missing, and see at a glance what you can cook with what's already at home.

FEATURES

📖 Recipes — Save your recipes with photos and step-by-step instructions.
🛒 Shopping — Build your shopping list from your recipes and tick items off as you go.
🥫 Storage — Keep track of the ingredients you have at home and their quantities.
🏷️ Tags — Organize recipes and groceries with tags and quick filters to find things fast.
📈 Charts — See what you cooked, which ingredients went into it, and the calories behind it all.
☁️ Syncing — Keep your data available on all your devices.

GETTING STARTED

1. Create recipes
Add a title, a photo, and steps with their ingredients. Groceries you create are shared across all recipes and live in the Groceries screen. Each grocery has a normal amount — the quantity you'd typically buy it in — which ReciPath uses to work out how much you need to purchase. Add a unit conversion and nutritional values for accurate dashboard data; the scan button in the top right fills in most of it for you.
2. Start shopping
Swipe a recipe or tap the cart button to enter shopping mode. Select the recipes you plan to cook, and every ingredient is added to your shopping list automatically. Your past trips stay available in the shopping history.
3. Keep track of what you have
Everything you tick off your list is added to your storage. The Recipe and Shopping screens highlight ingredients you already have at home, so you always know what you can cook and what still needs to be bought.
4. Start cooking
Open a recipe and start the timer while you cook. ReciPath records your time and shows the average cooking time for each recipe.

Want to see what makes the app tick? ReciPath is on GitHub!

quotes.text:
I built ReciPath because most recipe apps today have high monthly costs, overbearing social features, and require an internet connection just to see a shopping list.

THE APPROACH:
I’m primarily a Flutter developer. For this project, I wanted to experiment with a "database-driven UI" flow. Instead of heavy state management boilerplate, the UI state is tightly coupled to a local Drift (SQLite) DB. If it's in the DB, it's in the UI.

TECHNICAL HIGHLIGHTS:

- Offline First: Everything works locally. Accounts are optional and only used for syncing via Supabase.
- Shopping Planner: You select recipes, and the app generates a shopping list.
- Smart Timers: When you start a recipe, it tracks your actual cooking time to provide better averages later. It also handles per-step timers (e.g., a 60-minute oven timer) with local notifications and sounds.
- The Sharing Challenge: Since the app is self-contained, sharing recipes is currently done via JSON files. The hard part is mapping imported "grocery items" to local ones. The app tries to match by barcode and name, but I’d love to hear ideas on how to streamline this mapping process.

ROADMAP: BYOT AI INTEGRATION

- I'm currently looking into adding "Bring Your Own Token" AI support. The goal is to let users use their own API keys (OpenRouter/OpenAI/etc.) to import recipes directly from messy URLs or photos of physical cookbooks. Since recipe sites change their HTML constantly, using LLMs for schema mapping feels like the most robust …
